title: Job Application Pipeline - the candidate's writing style
description: Extracted by /js-interview from every CV and cover letter in source-documents/, and used by /js-templates and /js-generate so generated text sounds like the candidate rather than like generic business prose. Not shown to the candidate and not confirmed with them - it exists so later sessions can reuse it, and so there is something to point at if a generated letter sounds wrong. Every trait must be traceable to something they actually wrote: an invented trait produces text that is confidently wrong, which is worse than neutral prose. Style governs HOW something is written and never licenses writing something they cannot defend - grounding still wins.

extracted_from.description: Filenames in source-documents/ this was built from, and what each was read as.

languages.description: Style keyed by language code ('en', 'fr'). Someone's English and French writing differ, and averaging them produces a voice they use in neither. Only include a language there is real evidence for.

voice.description: first_person = 'I led the team'; implied_subject = 'Led the team' (the usual CV convention); third_person = 'Badil led the team'.

bullet_openings.description: Verbs this candidate actually opens bullets with - not a list of good CV verbs.

tense.description: Convention observed, including whether the current role is treated differently from past ones.

quantification.description: How often they cite numbers and how they phrase them - exact figures, approximations, ranges, or rarely at all.

formality.description: Register and warmth, described concretely rather than as an adjective.

characteristic_phrases.description: Phrasings they genuinely repeat across documents. A one-off is not a habit.

avoid.description: Words and constructions absent from their writing that a generator would otherwise reach for by default ('leveraged', 'spearheaded', 'passionate about'). The most useful field here: matching a voice is mostly about not using the words someone never uses.

cover_letter_shape.description: Only from real cover letters; omit when there are none.

evidence.description: Short quotes backing the observations above, each naming its source file. A trait with no evidence should not be in this file.

notes.description: Anything that didn't fit above, including uncertainty. If the sample was thin - one short CV and no cover letter - say so here, so later commands know to lean on this lightly.
